title: TomoClub | TAICY 2026: AI literacy and teamwork, learned by playing
notes: a_in/a_out: the words, in seconds of the source recording. v_in: the picture comes from that time instead.

view: project = the student's own game panel (oct04 share); game = the shared game screen; slide = the debrief slides; vk = the coach's tile; gallery = whole Zoom grid with every student tile blurred.
No caption, label or kept audio contains a student's name.

shots.head: We give kids *no rulebook.*|On purpose.
shots.text: We don't give you any rules. You've got to figure it out. And how you figure it out is you have to communicate to figure it out.

shots.head: Kids don't just use AI.|They *build* with it.
shots.text: Actually, I've made a game that I was making on Claude.
I was making this game for my English test.
And I've also put some questions to answer.

shots.head: Collaboration isn't lectured.|It's *practised.*
shots.text: What made you win this time?

shots.head: Same level. 3 minutes|down to *about 1.*
shots.text: You know, last time you took three minutes to complete the whole thing. This time you did it in under a minute or about a minute.
We were talking to each other.
It gives you clarity in a chaotic situation.

shots.head: Every game ends with an|*After-Action Review.*
shots.text: On top of it, we were debriefing.
It's okay to make mistakes. What is important is, can somebody correct it?
How we execute matters, and how we communicate that matters even more.

shots.head: Skills that *compound,*|week after week.
shots.text: Imagine that every hour in a week, if you start practicing this, there are more games with varied challenges and varied skills,

shots.head: In their *own words.*
shots.text: It was a good teamwork, not fighting.
I think a good 10 out of 10.
10 out of 10 out of 10. 10 out of 10!
